clinical_knowledge.topic: Moderate-to-Severe Acne Vulgaris evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Moderate-to-Severe Acne Vulgaris is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes an evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Acne Vulgaris, moderate-to-severe papulopustular/nodular, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Moderate-to-Severe Acne Vulgaris.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Rosacea without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Deep scarring already present — signals need for more aggressive treatment sooner.
management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Acne Vulgaris, moderate-to-severe papulopustular/nodular: assess pregnancy status before prescribing, then prescribe oral Doxycycline 100mg daily, topical Retinoid (Adapalene), and Benzoyl peroxide
Discuss Isotretinoin (Accutane) criteria and iPLEDGE if refractory
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.plan: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Acne Vulgaris, moderate-to-severe papulopustular/nodular. Before prescribing doxycycline or a topical retinoid, assess pregnancy status and pregnancy intentions; avoid these medicines during pregnancy. If appropriate, prescribe oral doxycycline with topical adapalene and benzoyl peroxide, limiting antibiotic duration. Discuss isotretinoin for severe or refractory disease; it requires strict pregnancy-prevention and monitoring requirements. Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling.
